annotations.title: Read the panchang for a date and place

description:
Computes the panchang for one civil date at one place: tithi, nakshatra with pada, yoga and karana, EACH WITH THE UTC AND LOCAL INSTANTS IT BEGINS AND ENDS, plus vara, sunrise, sunset, day length and the lunar month (amanta and purnimanta). The end times are usually what the user wants. Send a place, or lat and lon.

DELEGATE THIS RATHER THAN DERIVING IT: a tithi is the interval in which the Moon gains twelve degrees on the Sun, 20-26.8 hours (mean 23.6), and the civil day it names is set by the tithi running AT THAT PLACE'S SUNRISE, so two cities' panchangs for one date can differ by a whole tithi. Nakshatra about 20.8 to 27.2 hours, yoga about 19.5 to 25.2 hours, karana about 10 to 13.4 hours. A latitude with no sunrise that day is refused.

CITATION: required. See server instructions.

date.description: Civil date at the place, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, 1700-2200. Example: "2026-09-20". Omit: today (UTC).

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "28.6139". Send with lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "77.209". It sets the sunrise the whole panchang is read at.

place.description: Town or city with region or country. Example: "Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India". REQUIRED unless lat and lon are sent; an ambiguous name is refused with candidates.

tz.description: IANA zone or numeric UTC offset hours, for printing local times only. Example: "Asia/Kolkata".

name: compute_panchang
title: Read the panchang for a date and place
